items.title: Al Gallodoro Interview, 1966-05-10
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] This was the one Sal Franzella used to talk about... Adrian Fresh? [INTERVIEWEE] Adrian Fresh? Possibly. He's probably deceased now.

ctx.x: Well, when the theater closed in 1933, when the Orphean closed with Vortemul, rather, the other way with Vortemul, I decided to go to New York. In New York, I stopped in Philadelphia first. I don't know how long you want this story to be, but you can always cut it down, right? Oh, John. I stopped, yes. I stopped in Philadelphia to see a trumpet player from New Orleans. To be exact, his name was Danny Rhyne. R-Y-N. Danny Rhyne. And Philadelphia, I found out he was working in Atlantic City. He greeted me…

This was the one Sal Franzella used to talk about. Instead of talking about anyone, he would always talk about your ability as a saxophonist and clarinet. Is that the one he had great admiration for your performance and playing? Adrian Fresh?

Adrian Fresh? Possibly. He's probably deceased now. But when I got to Atlantic City, George Olsen had left the night before. So I was more or less stuck. But I saw that next door to the hotel that Olsen was in, Isham Jones. I-A-I-S-H-A-M. Isham Jones. He was some composer. He was a multi-millionaire when he passed away at Turkey Ranch. He wrote all of those beautiful tunes like Swinging Down the Lane and things like that. Anyway, I went to see his manager and he was interested in what I had to say. He gave me an…
